questions.stem: When ammonium chloride is heated in an open tube, the white solid disappears completely. When heated in a sealed tube, it only partially disappears. Why?

options.text: The sealed tube contains no oxygen for the reaction
In the open tube the gaseous products escape, preventing the reverse reaction; in the sealed tube the gases stay and can recombine
Different chemical reactions occur in open and sealed tubes
The sealed tube gets hotter, preventing decomposition

questions.explanation: In an open tube, the NH₃ and HCl gases produced by decomposition escape, so the reverse reaction cannot occur and the solid disappears completely. In a sealed tube, the gases cannot escape and can recombine to reform NH₄Cl when the tube cools, so the solid only partially disappears.
